title: Troubleshoot alarm 254 spindle motor overheat on a Haas mill
scope: Alarm 254 troubleshooting as demonstrated in SRC_HAAS_0010.

symptoms: alarm 254 spindle motor overheat during a job

machine_family.note: The narration distinguishes vertical and horizontal mills.

subsystem.note: Named in the title and narration.

symptoms.note: Stated in the narration and shown on the control.

alarm_codes.note: Stated in the narration and shown on the control.

components.note: Named in the narration or shown with labels on screen.

machine_model.note: Not stated; the video shows a VF-2 model graphic only as an illustration.

context.text: The presenter says the alarm can come up in the middle of a job, and names it as alarm 254 spindle motor overheat.
context.explanation: The captions state this directly. Cue 1 is corrected from 'alarmed 2:54 spin the motor overheat' to 'alarm 254 spindle motor overheat' (the video's title).

context.text: The control shows an orange banner reading '254 SPINDLE MOTOR OVERHEAT'.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Control screen with an orange banner '254 SPINDLE MOTOR OVERHEAT'.
evidence.explanation: The banner text is legible in the frame.

context.explanation: The narration around this moment names the alarm and how it is triggered.

rationale.text: The presenter says the spindle motor has a temperature sensor built into it, usually in the junction box, with factory-preset temperature limits, and that the sensor triggers alarm 254 when the motor temperature begins to reach those limits.
rationale.explanation: The captions state this directly. Cue 4 is corrected from 'alarm to 54' to 'alarm 254'.

questions.question: What does the machine do when the alarm triggers (stop the spindle, stop the program)? The video does not say.

action.text: The presenter says to begin by checking that the spindle loads are not way over a hundred percent for extended periods.
The Main Spindle panel shows spindle speed 2700 RPM, spindle power 18.7 KW and a Spindle Load bar reading 149%.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Main Spindle panel: spindle speed 2700 RPM, spindle power 18.7 KW, Spindle Load bar reading 149%.
evidence.explanation: The panel values and the load percentage are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about spindle load going well over a hundred percent.

rationale.text: The presenter ties spindle load that stays far over a hundred percent for long periods to running a long, super-aggressive program.

questions.question: What load level and duration are acceptable? The video only says 'not way over a hundred percent for extended periods'.

rationale.text: The presenter says this alarm can be triggered if there are problems with the spindle fan.

acceptance_criteria.text: The presenter says the fan should turn on as soon as the spindle starts turning.

The presenter says that on a vertical mill the fan should pull air up through the spindle head and push it out through the top, and on a horizontal mill it pushes air out through the back of the spindle head.

action.text: The presenter says that if the fan is working, to make sure it is running in the right direction.
A close-up shows a fan inside a sheet-metal housing.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Close-up of a fan inside a sheet-metal housing, shown while the spindle fan is discussed.
evidence.explanation: The fan housing and its blades are visible in the frame; the frame alone does not show that this is the spindle fan.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about the spindle fan turning on.

questions.question: How is the fan's direction checked in practice (by hand over the outlet, by eye)?

steps.title: Next-gen control: check the P39 cable

condition.text: The presenter says this check applies if the machine has a next-gen control.

action.text: The presenter says to open the control cabinet and look at the cable connected to P39 on the I/O PC board.
A technician crouches at an open control cabinet, with drives, boards and a 40 horsepower vector drive visible.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: A technician crouches at an open control cabinet; drives, boards and a 40 horsepower vector drive are visible.
evidence.explanation: The open cabinet and its contents are visible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about opening the control cabinet.

action.text: A 3D model of a circuit board shows a connector labelled 'P39'.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: 3D model of a circuit board with the connector labelled 'P39'.
evidence.explanation: The 'P39' label is legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment names P39 on the I/O PC board.

acceptance_criteria.text: The presenter says the cable should have a ferrite filter on it.

questions.question: What does the ferrite filter do for this alarm?

action.text: The presenter says to remove the spindle head cover and examine the temperature sensor itself.
A close-up shows a black cable labelled 'THERM PROBE' clamped to a brass fitting.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Close-up of a black cable labelled 'THERM PROBE' clamped to a brass fitting.
evidence.explanation: The cable label and brass fitting are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about examining the temperature sensor and its cable.

acceptance_criteria.text: The presenter says to make sure the sensor is not damaged and the cable is firmly connected.

steps.title: Contact the service outlet if the alarm persists

condition.text: The presenter says this applies if the alarm persists after these checks.
condition.explanation: The captions state this directly. Cue 14 is corrected from 'local hospital outlet' to 'local HFO' (the description says 'contact your local HFO').

action.text: The presenter says it is time to contact the local HFO for assistance.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected as above.

claim.text: The presenter makes the P39 cable check conditional on the machine having a next-gen control.
The presenter ends the checks with a hand-off to the local HFO if the alarm persists.
